entities.summary:
Jean (Jehan) Rolin (1408–1483) was a French bishop and Cardinal. He played a crucial role in the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages, serving as Bishop of Avignon from 1447 until his death in 1483. Rolin was a key figure in the Western Schism, a period of division within the Church that lasted from 1378 to 1417.

Rolin's tenure as Bishop of Avignon was marked by his efforts to reform the Church and promote the interests of the French monarchy. He was a strong supporter of the papacy and worked to strengthen the Church's ties with the French nobility.

Despite his efforts, Rolin's legacy is complex and contested. Some historians view him as a power-hungry cleric who exploited his position for personal gain, while others see him as a dedicated servant of the Church who worked tirelessly to promote its teachings.

Rolin's death in 1483 marked the end of an era in the Catholic Church, but his legacy continues to be felt in the modern world. His commitment to the Church and his role in shaping its history make him an important figure in the annals of religious history.

A striking statistic about Rolin is that he was one of the most powerful clergy in Europe during his lifetime, with significant control over the Church's finances and personnel.

As Cardinal, Rolin was known for his piety and his dedication to the Church's teachings. He was a strong advocate for the use of indulgences, a practice that allowed the faithful to purchase forgiveness for their sins.

In conclusion, Jean Rolin's legacy is a testament to the complex and often fraught history of the Catholic Church. His commitment to the Church and his role in shaping its history make him an important figure in the annals of religious history.
